speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: 'I dragged you in by the collar, and I've torn up the correction fee they'd have charged you. Drink. Then we can talk about this habit you have of arriving unconscious.'
after: 'Dragged you in by the collar. Tore up the correction fee they'd have charged you. Drink that, and then you can tell me why you keep arriving unconscious.'

speaker: (narration)
before: You knock three times. The manhole opens to a hand and a tired voice: 'Down you come.'
after: You knock three times, and the manhole opens on a hand and a tired voice that says, 'Down you come.'

speaker: (narration)
before: You cut the big black cable that feeds the facade's lights from the wheels. A spark; a silence. Far off, the perfect lamps flicker, stutter and come back on: {villain} keeps a very small private generator, just for himself.
after: You cut the big black cable from the wheels to the facade's lights. There is a spark, then silence, and far off the perfect lamps flicker and come back on: {villain} keeps a small private generator, just for himself.

speaker: (narration)
before: You pull the lever and ask the Perfect Nutrient Paste Dispenser for a refund. It chokes, burps and covers itself in a bright green foam that smells, fatally, of actual cabbage. A paste machine is not supposed to remember cabbage.
after: You pull the lever and ask the Perfect Nutrient Paste Dispenser for a refund. It chokes, burps and covers itself in green foam that smells, fatally, of real cabbage. A paste machine is not supposed to remember cabbage.

speaker: (narration)
before: Then a shoot, as thin as a thread, noses out of the dirt. And another. And a flower, the colour of everything the Capital is not.
after: Then a shoot as thin as a thread noses out of the dirt, and then another, and then a flower the colour of everything the Capital is not.

speaker: (narration)
before: 'Please take a number.' You take a number. It says 4,112,009.
after: 'Please take a number,' she says, so you take one, and it says 4,112,009.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Height inspection! Stand against the post, please, and straighten up.
after: Height inspection! Stand against the post for me, please, and straighten up as far as you are able.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Not that straight. Hm... you are one hair above regulation.
after: No, not as straight as that, that is worse. Now you are one hair above regulation, and the form only has the two boxes on it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: One hair, I will let go, this time. Please do not grow while you are inside.
after: I will let one hair go, this once, because nobody has ever told me what a hair counts as. Only please do not grow while you are inside, or I shall be the one who has to explain it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Still one hair above regulation. I have thought about that hair all week. Do not make me regret it.
after: You are still one hair above regulation. I have thought about that hair all week, and I looked for it in the manual, and it is not in there, so please do not make me regret it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Queue management! This is the approved queue, and you are already in it.
after: Queue management! This is the approved queue, and I am pleased to tell you that you are already standing in it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: You are not allowed to leave the queue. You are not allowed to join the queue. I do not understand it either.
after: You are not allowed to leave the queue, and you are not allowed to join it either, which I grant you is awkward. I have read the rule four times and I do not understand it any better than you do.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Still queueing? Good. You have a gift for remaining eligible.
after: Still queueing, I see, and very nicely too. You have a real gift for remaining eligible, and I would write that down for you if there were a box for it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: It is a long queue. It is the best queue we have.
after: It is a long queue, I know, but it is the best one we have, and between ourselves I have never seen where the front of it goes.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. You wish to leave? But you have not finished arriving. Please arrive first.
after: Exit control. You wish to leave? I am sorry, but according to this you have not finished arriving yet, and I cannot let anyone out who is not properly in. Please arrive first.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. This is the exit. It is also the entrance. It is also, from some angles, a wall.
after: Exit control. This is the exit, and it is also the entrance, and they told me on my first day that from some angles it is a wall. I try not to stand at those angles.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. You are, I think, still inside. Congratulations.
after: Exit control. As far as I can tell you are still inside, so congratulations, I suppose, unless it is commiserations. Nobody has told me which.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for departing the most perfect place in the kingdom?
after: Exit Interview Booth, good day. May I take your name, and your reason for departing the most perfect place in the kingdom?

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: 'It is not perfect' is not an approved answer. Nor is pointing at something while saying it.
after: I am afraid 'it is not perfect' is not one of the approved answers, and neither is pointing at something while you say it. I do not choose the answers. I am not certain anybody does.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Your departure request has been received. It has been filed under 'Dissent'. It will be looked at in four to six years.
after: Your departure request has been received and filed under 'Dissent', which is the only drawer I was given. Somebody will look at it in four to six years, and I do hope for both our sakes that it is not me.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: That is also good. That is the best.
after: Yesterday was also very good, so I am quite confident about tomorrow. It is restful, knowing in advance.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Welcome to {showcase}! Houses, lawns, a small round approved fountain. Everything you could want. Everything you may want.
after: Welcome to {showcase}! We have houses, and lawns, and a small round approved fountain, which is everything you could want. It is also everything you may want, so that works out very nicely.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Sometimes I go behind the house and look at the wall. Just the wall. Nobody has told me I cannot. Please do not tell them.
after: (a whisper) Sometimes I go round behind the house and look at the wall. It is only a wall, but nobody has told me how to feel about it. Please do not tell them I go.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Once. I wish it would again.
after: (a whisper) It was only the once, and I think it was a mistake. I stand under it most mornings all the same, in case it makes another.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Thursday! Five minutes of spontaneity, permit ready! I have rehearsed being caught off guard.
after: It is Thursday! I have my permit ready for my five minutes of spontaneity, and I have rehearsed being caught off guard all week, so I expect to do it very well.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card. The kind with nothing written in it.
after: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card, one of the kind with nothing written in it.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: There is a door at the back that does not open. I think there is a world on the other side. I think it is raining.
after: (a whisper) There is a door at the back that does not open. I put my ear to it sometimes. I think there is a world on the other side, and I think it is raining there.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The portrait is looking at me. It is always looking at me. It is very kind of him to look.
after: The portrait is looking at me. It is always looking at me, wherever I stand on the lawn, and it is very kind of him to take the trouble.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I would never look away. I cannot.
after: I would never look away, of course. (a small laugh) I did try it once, and I cannot.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: He is never here, you know. He has never once come down. Only the portraits come.
after: (a pause, then quietly) He is never here, you know. In all these years he has not once come down to see us. Only the portraits come.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The portraits do all the looking. It is all done by portrait.
after: The portraits do all the looking for him. It is all done by portrait, and lately I have begun to think that must be lonely.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens! Today is a PERFECT day! The weather is APPROVED!
after: Great news, citizens! Today is a PERFECT day! The weather is APPROVED, and I am delighted to confirm that it was my own office that approved it!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! Lost Ministry property must be returned at once, and not spoken to!
after: Do please continue to be happy, as scheduled! And one small reminder: lost Ministry property must be returned at once, and must on no account be spoken to!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens! A reminder that smiling is MANDATORY! Those found frowning will be helped! Thank you for your cooperation!
after: Attention, citizens! A friendly reminder that smiling is MANDATORY! Anyone found frowning will be helped, promptly and at some length, and will thank us for it afterwards!

speaker: Wren
before: Keep your head down and your hope up. Hope's unapproved. Carry it anyway.
after: Keep your head down, and carry your hope anyway. It has never once been approved.

speaker: Wren
before: He likes things perfect. We like things alive. Keep moving.
after: Whatever you see up there, tell me exactly. It all goes into the record, in ink.

speaker: Kestrel
before: Guards change on the hour. I change whenever I like. Keep up.
after: Psst. Guards change on the hour and I change whenever I feel like it, so keep up.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: 27-B needs 27-C. 27-C needs 27-B. I keep both forms beside his chair.
after: I do beg your pardon. I was only telling my husband what the weather's doing.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Back in the Gainlands... we threw commuters. Now I'd pay... to be thrown.
after: Back in the Gainlands... my crews got rest days. I'd like... those back.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: I am designing a drain. It will not be perfect. I am learning to let that be.
after: I am designing a drain. It will not be perfect, and I am learning to let that be.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: Good day. I owe you rather more than that. I am told it is a start.
after: Good day. I owe you rather more than a good day, but I am told it is a start.

speaker: Isla Brannoch
before: Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually.
after: Dad says hi. Well, he said 'Hm', but I've had years to learn the language.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: 'You fell over, so we rolled you in. The fee's still yours, mind. The tea isn't free just because the kingdom is.'
after: 'You fell over, so we rolled you in. No fee. There never was one, down here. Sit up slowly and drink the tea.'

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Good day! A good day! The weather is whatever it wants!
after: Good day! And I mean it's really a good one, I'm not just reporting it. The weather's doing whatever it wants, and I didn't even check first.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I don't know the approved hat size and I don't care! It's wonderful to be alive.
after: I got rained on this morning and I complained about it to a total stranger, and she complained right back. It was wonderful.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I am going to wear a hat of any size. Maybe two at once.
after: I'm going to wear a hat of whatever size I like, and I might wear two at once. I haven't decided yet, and I'm enjoying not having decided.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Berta. Berta. Berta. It is a very good name.
after: Berta. I keep saying it to hear how it sounds. Berta. Do you know, it's a very good name, and I think my mother chose it.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: My cheeks do not hurt any more. My cheeks are mine.
after: My cheeks don't hurt any more. They're mine again, and I rested them all of yesterday by frowning at a pigeon.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Visitors come! Real ones! They are mostly confused, but they come.
after: We get visitors now, real ones! They're mostly lost and a bit confused, but they come, and I don't smile at them until I've decided whether I like them.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Spontaneity every day! I am exhausted! I am not sure I like it! I love it!
after: It's spontaneity every day now, and I'm exhausted! I'm honestly not sure I like it. No, I do, I love it. I'm allowed to change my mind now, you see.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Every hat size! All of them! Come and see the hats!
after: We have every hat size now, all of them at once! Come and see the hats. My daughter's trying them all on, and she says most of them are terrible.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The portraits are coming down. There is a lot of wall behind them. Nobody knows what to put there.
after: The portraits are coming down, and there's a great deal of wall behind them. Nobody can agree what to put there instead, which is the best part.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Please do whatever you like. That is all.
after: So please do whatever you like today. I have nothing further to announce, and I find, rather to my surprise, that I do not mind.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. A reminder: you do not have to smile. (a pause) Also: you may smile. We are very easy.
after: Attention, citizens. A reminder that you do not have to smile. (a pause) You may, of course, if something strikes you. We are very easy about it these days.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now every day. You may stop rehearsing your surprise.
after: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now every day. You may stop rehearsing your surprise. I am told the real kind needs no practice.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. All is not well yet, but it will be.
after: Attention, citizens. All is not well. I am told that I may say so now. All is not well yet, but it is getting better.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: It is a lot of work. Thank you for helping.
after: It is a great deal of work, and I notice it is mostly you who are doing it. Thank you. This has been... well. This has been Percival.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: They are in the cellar. There is tea.
after: They are in the cellar, and there is tea. I am told I would be welcome, which is generous of them, and I have not yet found the nerve to go down.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: I used to measure people. Now I just look at them. A man walked past yesterday who was nine feet tall and I said 'good morning'.
after: I used to measure people, and now I just look at them, which takes a lot less time. A man walked past yesterday who must have been nine feet tall, and all I said to him was 'good morning'.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: I am not myself. I am much better.
after: I'm not myself at all. I think I might be somebody better. I've still got the stick, mind, and I don't know where you go to hand a stick in.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Come in, come in. Bring any height.
after: Come in, come in, and bring whatever height you've got. I've stopped keeping count, and I sleep much better for it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Still no queue. I am doing very well.
after: There's still no queue. I did go for that walk, by the way. I got as far as the fountain and came back, but I'm doing very well.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. You may leave whenever you like; I'm only standing here. It's a very open exit.
after: Exit control, or it was. You can leave whenever you like now, and I'm only standing here because it turns out I'm rather fond of the view. It's a very open exit.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. Goodbye. Come back. Goodbye.
after: Exit control. Goodbye, and do come back, won't you? I never used to be allowed to say that part, so I'm saying it to everyone.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. This is an exit. It is also an entrance. It is, from every angle, a door.
after: Exit control. Well, this is an exit, and it's an entrance as well, and I walked the whole way round it this morning and from every angle it's a door.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: A door. A good door.
after: It's only a door, isn't it? It's a good door, though. I think I'll go on standing by it for a bit, if nobody minds.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for leaving?
after: Exit Interview Booth. Name, and reason for... no, I'm sorry, that just comes out by itself. You don't need a reason any more.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: ...I was never going to read the answers. Please go and have a nice day.
after: I was never going to read the answers anyway, and nor was anybody else. Please go wherever you like, and have a nice day while you're about it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Have a nice day.
after: Have a nice day. I mean it now, which is new, so I'm still getting used to how it sounds.
